learningObjective: Identify correct statements about ONNX shape inference and its role in deployment.

canonicalClaims.claim: ONNX shape inference is a static, per-op procedure driven by operator schemas; it propagates shapes and dtypes and leaves symbolic dimensions when they depend on runtime tensors. Inferred shapes enable downstream buffer planning and kernel selection.
conditions: Model uses ops with published shape-inference in the declared opset.
Consumer respects the produced value_info metadata.
nonImplications: Does not imply full concretization; symbolic dims are supported.
Does not imply every custom op has shape inference.

misconceptions.claim: Exported ONNX contains no intermediate shape metadata.
misconceptions.whyWrong: ONNX files include value_info entries where known.

misconceptions.claim: Shape inference resolves all symbolic dimensions at export.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic axes such as batch and seq_len are intentionally left symbolic.

misconceptions.claim: Shape inference is a runtime-only concern.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a static analysis defined by op schemas that many tools consume ahead of time.

misconceptions.claim: Downstream compilers cannot use ONNX shape info.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TensorRT, ORT and others rely on it for buffer planning and kernel selection.
